title: PathCal: State-Aware Reflection-Marker Calibration for Efficient Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2605.23074v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Large Reasoning Language Models (LRMs) tackle complex tasks through test-time scaling, generating long-form Chain-of-Thought (CoT) trajectories during inference. These trajectories contain reflection markers such as wait, but, and alternatively, accompanying hesitation, revision, and alternative explorations. Recent test-time control methods use these markers to steer reasoning, but treating them as one coarse-grained category can obscure their distinct intervention effects. We study how marker identity and reasoning context shape these effects. Type-wise suppression produces different accuracy--length tradeoffs, while fixed-prefix interventions show that the relative benefit of continuation and revision varies across prefixes and tasks. translated_title: PathCal：面向高效推理的状态感知反思标记校准
translated_abstract: 大型推理语言模型（LRMs）通过测试时扩展来解决复杂任务，在推理过程中生成长篇的思维链（CoT）轨迹。这些轨迹中包含诸如“wait”、“but”和“alternatively”等反思标记，伴随着犹豫、修订和替代性探索。近期的测试时控制方法利用这些标记来引导推理，但将它们视为一个粗粒度的类别可能会掩盖它们各自不同的干预效果。我们研究了标记类型和推理上下文如何塑造这些效果。按类型进行抑制会产生不同的准确率-长度权衡，而固定前缀干预表明，延续与修订的相对收益会因前缀和任务的不同而变化。受这些发现启发，我们提出了PathCal，这是一个无需训练的控制器，它利用延续、修订与替代性探索之间的瞬时竞争来调整固定延续偏置的强度……
tldr: 该论文发现不同反思标记的干预效果各异，并据此提出无需训练的PathCal控制器，通过实时感知延续、修订与替代探索之间的竞争状态来动态校准延续偏置强度，从而提升大型推理语言模型的推理效率。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes PathCal, a training-free test-time controller that dynamically calibrates a fixed continuation bias based on the instantaneous competition among continuation, revision, and alternative exploration, enabling more efficient reasoning in large reasoning language models.
